$MU Trade Idea: Oct 28 800P

Level to watch: 853 ✅
Targets: 821, 734 🎯
Invalidation: sustained reclaim of 853 🛑

853 is the line I'm watching.

If buyers lose it, 821 could come into play next.

Big week for memory stocks:

$SKHY reports Tuesday evening U.S. time.

$SNDK reports Thursday after the close.

Both could influence sentiment toward $MU.

I'm watching their outlooks on memory pricing, demand, and margins, and how stocks actually react.

Here's my plan:

853: Buyers need to defend this level. A break below followed by a failed reclaim would put the bearish setup in focus.

821: First downside target. Watch whether buyers step in or the bounce gets sold.

734: If 821 fails and $SNDK gets a negative earnings reaction Thursday, this becomes the deeper downside level I'm watching. It's conditional, not an automatic target.

If 853 fails and rejects the retest, MU Oct 28 800P could work for a quick downside move.

A sustained reclaim of 853 invalidates that breakdown setup.

Those puts expire Wednesday, BEFORE Sandisk reports Thursday.

They're a separate short-term trade, not a way to play that earnings reaction.

Size for the full premium risk and take profits along the way.

No need to front-run the breakdown.

If buyers defend 853, respect it.

Let the level fail first. Then trade the reaction.

Options carry risk of loss. Not financial advice.

zh_summary: Not actively trading. Pointing out Neocloud/Colo financing issues since 2025 from $SLNH to $CRWV. Only a few neoclouds survive long-term with moat vs hyperscalers. Nuances to Elon's comments; $NBIS has better SOFR+2.75% $3.5B Citibank facility. Concerns if amplifying competitor downfall benefits $SPCX + $TSLA. @aleabitoreddit
en_summary: Not actively trading. Pointing out Neocloud/Colo financing issues since 2025 from $SLNH to $CRWV. Only a few neoclouds survive long-term with moat vs hyperscalers. Nuances to Elon's comments; $NBIS has better SOFR+2.75% $3.5B Citibank facility. Concerns if amplifying competitor downfall benefits $SPCX + $TSLA. @aleabitoreddit
text:
Not actively. I've been pointing out issues with Neocloud/Colo financing since 2025 from $SLNH to $CRWV debt interest. 

And maintain my opinion only a few neoclouds would survive in a few years, given they build enough of a moat to differentiate themselves against hyperscalers. 

So I don't think Elon's comments are completely wrong about Neoclouds, but there's nuances. 

One example was $NBIS SOFR + 2.75% $3.5B facility with Citibank, which actually has better rates than GPU financing from $2T+ companies. 

So kinda hard to say neocloud financing has "entirely shut off" since this Citibank facility was announced 3D ago

I'm not arguing the merits of Elon's claims here. There's some truth to them, even if they're framed in extremes.

I'm happy to hear his opinion on the direction of the industry... but if they're mainly amplifying concerns about competitor downfall (which benefits $SPCX + $TSLA)

There's some cause for concern about how healthy that is to the town square dynamic Elon originally envisioned with X.

en_summary: @amitisinvesting thinks those two neoclouds have the best chance to survive, but says the $NBIS rate was likely a 365 day bridge loan, not 5 year convertibles. $CRWV could not get the same 9% rates as June today, per its yields, unless Jensen and Blackstone step in. Core issue: every neocloud must dilute or lever up to buy GPUs, and the market will not give cheaper rates.
text:
I think those are the two that will have the best chance at surviving

However that NBIS rate I believe was more like a bridge loan? Only 365 days, not actual 5-year convertible notes

CRWV debt being secondary does not matter because if they needed fresh capital today, they could not get the same 9% rates they got in June as per what their yields are implying

Unless Jensen and Blackstone step in

The fundamental issue is every single one of these clouds needs to dilute or lever the balance sheet to afford GPUs to resell them

and for whatever reason, the market isnt ready to give them cheaper rates anymore
